rv.q: The show is worth seeing for Neff's raw determination and I suspect it will deepen over time.
This superlative production is directed by Brit Jeremy Herrin, in a Chicago debut for the ages, providing 65 minutes of theater that’s both fun and disturbing.
It’s intoxicating to watch Neff and Gehlfuss go after one another.
Steppenwolf’s first show of 2025 is going to be hard to top.
Fool for Love is in exactly the right hands here, and it leaves the audience pondering just how much emotional wreckage one person's selfishness can create.

A wonderfully accomplished cast, Neff, Gehlfuss, Hopper and Chamberlain coat their characters in a potent realism; one that builds and nurtures both understanding and compassion—attributes that define superlative theater.
Now’s the time to savor the current moment of Steppenwolf confidently returning to Shepard as one of the company’s great and most important theatrical muses.
Presented in Steppenwolf’s more intimate downstairs theater, this is quite simply storytelling at its best.
In Director Jeremy Herrin’s stunning production, it’s a full on embrace of passion and hate, a bittersweet love story for fools.
Neff’s stunning, forceful performance sets the tempo for the entire cast.
One will find that hour full of passion and a fury all its own.
Yet on some level this play really doesn’t have very much to say aside from the fact that the intense interplay of a man and a woman can wreak havoc.
This is more than a play, it is indeed a theatrical experience...
I cannot in good conscience suggest that this is where my readers or podcast listeners should invest what might be limited theater dollars.

cn.t: Steppenwolf's revival of Shepard's toxic love story earns mostly strong reviews for its gritty intensity and stellar performances, though some critics find the 40-year-old play feels dated despite the production's heat.
